name: The DMZ and Panmunjom
region: Gyeonggi and Gangwon, north of Seoul
tagline: One of the most heavily guarded borders on earth, a four-kilometre strip of tunnels, observation posts and wildlife, an hour north of Seoul.
highlight: Looking across the border from an observatory at a landscape the two Koreas have watched each other across since 1953.
shortDescription: The Demilitarized Zone between North and South Korea, with tunnels, the Dora Observatory, Imjingak and, when open, the Joint Security Area at Panmunjom, visited on guided tours from Seoul.
metaDescription: A DMZ and Panmunjom travel guide: Imjingak, the Third Tunnel, Dora Observatory, the Joint Security Area, how to book tours from Seoul, rules, safety, history and a one-day plan.
nearestAirport: Incheon International (ICN), about 1.5 hours to Seoul then a tour
knownFor: The border, tunnels, observatories, Cold War history
goodFor: History and politics, unusual travel, day trips from Seoul

image.file: File:Peace Altar at Imjingak, Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), South Korea.jpg
image.alt: The Peace Altar at Imjingak near the Demilitarized Zone

intro: The Korean Demilitarized Zone is a strip of land about 250 km long and 4 km wide that cuts across the peninsula near the 38th parallel. It was set up by the armistice agreement of 1953, which halted the fighting of the Korean War without a peace treaty, and it remains a heavily guarded frontier, lined with fences, minefields and guard posts on both sides. Ironically, with few people allowed inside, it has also become a refuge for wildlife, including cranes and other rare birds.

For visitors, the DMZ is a strange, moving and sometimes tense place. Tours from Seoul usually visit Imjingak, a park with memorials and a bridge where prisoners were exchanged, one of the tunnels dug by North Korea under the border, and Dora Observatory, where binoculars look out over the North. Some tours reach the Joint Security Area at Panmunjom, where blue huts straddle the border and soldiers face each other, but access there is controlled and depends on the political situation, and is sometimes suspended.

You cannot visit the DMZ independently. Tours are run by the government-approved operators and the USO, they require a passport, and they have dress codes and rules about photos. Book ahead, follow instructions, and treat it with respect, since it is a place where a war remains unresolved and families are still separated.

whyVisit.intro: The DMZ is a memorable, thought-provoking day that puts the Korean story in context.

attractionsIntro: Tour routes vary, but most include some of these places.

attractions.name: Imjingak

image.file: File:Peace Altar at Imjingak, Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), South Korea.jpg
image.alt: The Peace Altar at Imjingak with memorial ribbons

attractions.text: A park near the border with memorials, a Peace Bell and the Freedom Bridge, where prisoners of war crossed in 1953. Ribbons and messages from separated families hang from the fences.
attractions.tip: Free to visit without a tour.

attractions.name: Dora Observatory

image.file: File:Dora Observatory, Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), South Korea.jpg
image.alt: The Dora Observatory viewing platform overlooking the border

attractions.text: An observation post where you can use binoculars to see the North's propaganda village and land beyond the border.
attractions.tip: Photography is limited to a line.

attractions.name: The Third Infiltration Tunnel

image.file: File:3RD INFILTRATION TUNNEL AT THE DMZ SOUTH KOREA OCT 2012 (8213209373).jpg
image.alt: The entrance to the Third Infiltration Tunnel at the DMZ

attractions.text: A tunnel discovered in 1978, dug by North Korea under the border, which you can walk down. It is low and steep, and helmets are required.
attractions.tip: Bring no large bags, and expect a stooping walk.

attractions.name: Joint Security Area (Panmunjom)

image.file: File:Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) Joint Security Area (JSA) Looking Into North Korea (28819154694).jpg
image.alt: The Joint Security Area at the DMZ looking toward North Korea

attractions.text: The blue conference huts on the border line, where soldiers of both sides stand face to face. Visits are strictly controlled and sometimes suspended.

attractions.name: Dorasan Station
attractions.text: A train station built for a hoped-for rail link to the North, and never used for regular passenger service.

attractions.name: DMZ Theater and Exhibition Hall
attractions.text: A museum about the DMZ's history and nature.

bestTime.headline: Spring and autumn
bestTime.summary: The DMZ is best visited in clear weather, since haze hides the North.
bestTime.avoid: Rainy or foggy days, and any time when tours are suspended.
